architecture.label: Architecture Gallery
architecture.description: 150 landmark architectural works from every civilization

objects.name: The Parthenon
objects.description: The Parthenon is a temple to the goddess Athena on the Acropolis of Athens. Built with perfect optical illusions—the columns are slightly curved and lean inward to appear perfectly straight—it represents the pinnacle of Doric Greek architecture. Originally brightly painted, it housed a colossal gold and ivory statue of Athena.
objects.significance: The definitive example of Classical Greek architecture and a symbol of democracy and Western civilization.
objects.fun_fact: The Parthenon has more optical corrections built into it than any other ancient building.
objects.image_hint: A marble temple with rows of Doric columns on a rocky hilltop
objects.educational_importance: Illustrates Art principles in architectural history.
objects.activity: Draw the floor plan or elevation of The Parthenon.

quiz.question: In which country is The Parthenon located?

objects.name: The Colosseum
objects.description: The Colosseum (Flavian Amphitheatre) could seat 50,000-80,000 spectators for gladiatorial contests, animal hunts, and public spectacles. Its elliptical design, vaulted arches, and complex underground tunnels (hypogeum) represent remarkable Roman engineering. The velarium awning protected spectators from sun.
objects.significance: The greatest example of Roman architecture and engineering, the model for all subsequent sports stadiums.
objects.fun_fact: The Colosseum was built by Jewish slaves from Jerusalem after the Roman destruction of the Temple.
objects.image_hint: An oval multi-tiered stone amphitheatre with arched openings, partially ruined
objects.educational_importance: Illustrates History principles in architectural history.
objects.activity: Draw the floor plan or elevation of The Colosseum.

quiz.question: In which country is The Colosseum located?

objects.name: The Pantheon
objects.description: The Pantheon is the best-preserved Roman building, featuring a concrete dome 43.3 meters in diameter—still the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome. The oculus (eye) at the dome's apex, 8.7 meters wide, is the only light source. The interior sphere fits a perfect 43.3m cube.
objects.significance: The world's best preserved ancient building and the model for domed architecture worldwide for 2,000 years.
objects.fun_fact: The Pantheon's dome was not surpassed in size for over 1,300 years.
objects.image_hint: A circular domed temple with a massive portico of Corinthian columns
objects.educational_importance: Illustrates Engineering principles in architectural history.
objects.activity: Draw the floor plan or elevation of The Pantheon.

quiz.question: In which country is The Pantheon located?

objects.name: Hagia Sophia
objects.architect: Anthemius of Tralles & Isidore of Miletus
objects.description: Hagia Sophia (Holy Wisdom) was for nearly a thousand years the world's largest cathedral. Its massive dome appears to float on a halo of 40 windows. It was converted to a mosque in 1453 and to a museum in 1934; in 2020, it became a mosque again.
objects.significance: The supreme achievement of Byzantine architecture and a model for Islamic mosque design worldwide.
objects.fun_fact: The dome appears to float because light enters between its base and the drum, creating an illusion of suspension.
objects.image_hint: A vast domed building with minarets, combining Byzantine and Ottoman architectural elements
objects.educational_importance: Illustrates Art principles in architectural history.
objects.activity: Draw the floor plan or elevation of Hagia Sophia.

quiz.question: In which country is Hagia Sophia located?

objects.name: Taj Mahal
objects.description: The Taj Mahal is a white marble mausoleum built by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan for his wife Mumtaz Mahal, who died in childbirth. It took 20,000 workers 22 years to complete. The complex uses perfect symmetry and is set in a charbagh (four-part paradise garden).
objects.significance: The supreme example of Mughal architecture and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, often called the most beautiful building in the world.
objects.fun_fact: The Taj Mahal changes color throughout the day—pinkish at dawn, white at midday, golden at sunset.
objects.image_hint: A white marble dome flanked by four minarets reflected in a long pool
objects.educational_importance: Illustrates Art principles in architectural history.
objects.activity: Draw the floor plan or elevation of Taj Mahal.

quiz.question: In which country is Taj Mahal located?

objects.name: Notre-Dame Cathedral
objects.architect: Jean de Chelles & Pierre de Montreuil
objects.description: Notre-Dame de Paris is the Gothic cathedral that defined medieval European architecture. Its flying buttresses allowed thinner walls and enormous stained glass windows. Severely damaged by fire in 2019, its restoration is underway.
objects.significance: The greatest example of French Gothic architecture, influencing cathedral building across Europe for centuries.
objects.fun_fact: Notre-Dame's spire was added in the 19th century; the medieval spire had been removed in 1786.
objects.image_hint: A Gothic cathedral with twin towers, rose windows, and flying buttresses
objects.educational_importance: Illustrates Art principles in architectural history.
objects.activity: Draw the floor plan or elevation of Notre-Dame Cathedral.

quiz.question: In which country is Notre-Dame Cathedral located?

objects.name: Alhambra Palace
objects.description: The Alhambra is a palace and fortress complex of the Nasrid sultans of Granada, featuring intricately carved stucco walls, geometric tile work, and muqarnas (honeycomb) ceilings. Its Court of the Lions features 124 marble columns surrounding an alabaster fountain.
objects.significance: The masterpiece of Moorish architecture in Spain, representing the Islamic world's sophistication in the 14th century.
objects.fun_fact: The name Alhambra means 'The Red One' in Arabic, referring to the reddish clay used in construction.
objects.image_hint: A palace with ornate carved stucco arches, geometric tilework, and courtyard gardens
objects.educational_importance: Illustrates Art principles in architectural history.
objects.activity: Draw the floor plan or elevation of Alhambra Palace.

quiz.question: In which country is Alhambra Palace located?

objects.name: Angkor Wat
objects.description: Angkor Wat is the world's largest religious monument, originally built as a Hindu temple dedicated to Vishnu, later converted to Buddhist use. Its five towers represent Mount Meru, the home of the gods. The walls bear over 1,000 square meters of narrative bas-relief sculpture.
objects.significance: The largest religious monument ever built and the architectural crown of the Khmer Empire.
objects.fun_fact: Angkor Wat appears on the Cambodian national flag—the only monument on any country's flag.
objects.image_hint: Five tower-spires rising from concentric galleries surrounded by a moat
objects.educational_importance: Illustrates Art principles in architectural history.
objects.activity: Draw the floor plan or elevation of Angkor Wat.

quiz.question: In which country is Angkor Wat located?

objects.name: Eiffel Tower
objects.description: Built as the entrance arch for the 1889 World's Fair, the Eiffel Tower was initially criticized as an 'iron monstrosity.' Standing 330 meters tall, it was the world's tallest man-made structure for 41 years. Its iron lattice design was revolutionary in demonstrating the aesthetic potential of industrial materials.
objects.significance: The most visited monument in the world and the defining symbol of iron construction and the industrial age.
objects.fun_fact: The Eiffel Tower grows taller in summer—heat causes the iron to expand by up to 15 cm.
objects.image_hint: A tapering iron lattice tower with four arched legs, Paris below
objects.educational_importance: Illustrates Engineering principles in architectural history.
objects.activity: Draw the floor plan or elevation of Eiffel Tower.

quiz.question: In which country is Eiffel Tower located?

objects.name: Forbidden City
objects.description: The Forbidden City was the Chinese imperial palace for 500 years, housing 24 emperors from the Ming and Qing dynasties. It contains 980 buildings covering 180 acres, aligned on a north-south axis. Ordinary citizens were forbidden to enter on pain of death, giving it its name.
objects.significance: The world's largest palace complex and the best preserved example of traditional Chinese imperial architecture.
objects.fun_fact: The Forbidden City has 9,999 rooms—legend says only Heaven could have 10,000.
objects.image_hint: A vast palace complex of red walls and golden roofs arranged on a central axis
objects.educational_importance: Illustrates Art principles in architectural history.
objects.activity: Draw the floor plan or elevation of Forbidden City.

quiz.question: In which country is Forbidden City located?
